short_description: BT-Cond PHOENIX atmospheres, 44 % of SVO's set: Teff 800-6,600 K (SVO bt-cond, air wavelengths)
description: SVO's BT-COND grid: "The BT-COND Model grid of theoretical spectra. Brown dwarfs/extrasolar planets atmosphere models without irradiation and no dust opacity (no dust settling) but updated abundances. Wavelengths have been converted to air wavelengths." Teff 800-6,600 K, log g -0.5-6.0, [M/H] -4.0 to +0.5, [alpha/M] -0.2 to +0.6. A SUBSET: NJM holds 6,028 of the 13,648 spectra SVO lists (44 %). SVO refuses scripted downloads now, so it cannot be completed from SVO today. NJM serves no cube for it; clients build one (about 200 GB for the whole grid, mostly empty nodes).

notes: References: SVO's registry record credits 1999ApJ...512..377H; the Lyon README names Allard et al. (2012) as the refereed BT-Settl paper, and its bibcode 2012RSPTA.370.2765A is given from knowledge, not checked here. Bolometric flux: the lowest-gravity spectra (logg -0.5 and 0) hold only 0.38-0.60 of sigma*T^4; see bolometric_exceptions. Nill to confirm this is acceptable for listing.

bolometric_exceptions.why: BT-Cond's lowest-gravity models (logg -0.5 and 0) integrate to 0.38-0.60 of sigma*T^4 on their own 0.001 A - 10^7 A wavelengths, falling smoothly with gravity; measured 29 Oct 2026 on the guard's 120-spectrum sample (14 such spectra, all at logg <= 0). Not a unit error (that would be a constant 1/pi or 1/(4 pi)), and SED_Tools' cleaner only ever divides over-bright spectra; the headers declare SVO's own unit, unconverted. Not checked against raw SVO files: none on cirrus has these parameters. Treat fluxes there as unreliable
